chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no greeting (salam) in the prayer upon the deceased.
ai.seo_question: Does the funeral prayer include the concluding greeting of peace?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the funeral prayer (Salat al-Mayyit) is a supplication (dua) rather than a full ritual prayer, thereby lacking the concluding 'Taslim' (greeting of peace) found in other prayers. This ruling highlights the distinct jurisprudential status of Salat al-Mayyit in Shia fiqh, emphasizing its brevity and focus on intercession for the deceased. The narration, transmitted through prominent scholars like al-Halabi and Zurara, underscores the consensus on this specific procedural difference.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby and Zurara, 
from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both having said:
‘There is no greeting in the Salaat upon the deceased’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from al-Halabiy from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, have said, ‘
There is no Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) to end Salah (prayer) for a deceased.’”
